item.title: Amir Hajian (Awby Knowledge Studio Inc) — Wed Oct 21, 5:52 PM — IdeaLab
item.description:
Title: The Universal Tango:How AI and Physics are Rewriting the Rules of Scientific Discovery
Abstract: For decades, the relationship between artificial intelligence and physics has been largely one-sided: physicists built the hardware, and AI processed the data. Today, that dynamic has fundamentally shifted into a powerful, bidirectional symbiosis that is redefining both fields. This talk explores the cutting-edge convergence of AI and physics across three critical frontiers.
First, we examine how AI is revolutionizing physical modeling to accelerate traditional simulations by orders of magnitude, effectively breaking the computational bottleneck of classical physics.
Second, we flip the script to explore how physics is rescuing AI, turning hardware "noise" into a computational feature to design ultra-low-energy chips that perform AI inference natively.
Finally, we look to the future of the scientific method itself, the rise of "AI Scientists" and advanced knowledge-work agents. F

item.title: 👻 Ghost Tour: The Exhibition Grounds 🎡 — Thu Oct 22, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years! # 👻 Ghost Tour: The Exhibition Grounds 🎡
### Toronto's Haunted Fairgrounds, Dark History & One Building I Don't Like Being Near
The Exhibition Grounds have spent more than a century hosting crowds, celebrations, soldiers, shows, and some of Toronto's biggest events. But underneath all that history is a darker side.
The Exhibition Grounds are said to be **one of the most haunted places in Toronto** — and I'll be honest: **this is the one place on my ghost walks that genuinely scares me.**
There's something about the atmosphere here. Some buildings have an energy that feels different. And when you know what happened in them, it's hard not to look at them a little differently.
On this evening ghost walk, we'll explore the grounds and hear stories of **soldiers, settlers, performers, animals, tragedies, and people who may never have completely left.**

item.title: Baila Sáfica Film Screening and Social Dancing — Thu Oct 22, 7:00 PM — Glad Day (32 Lisgar)
item.description: We are excited to welcome y'all to our very first film screening of "La Salsa Vive" Baila Sáfica presents "La Salsa Vive": Telling the story of two cities bound by the rhythm of salsa, New York City and Cali, Colombia, La Salsa Vive is a vibrant cinematic exploration of the evolution of the style and a collective passion that has inspired generations. Featuring insights from salsa legends like singers Rubén Blades and Henry Fiol, percussionists Samuel Formell, Johnny "Dandy" Rodríguez and orchestra conductor Willie Rosario, and highlighting the dedicated dancers, music collectors, and enthusiastic youth who are united through music and dance, La Salsa Vive is a pulsating journey through a vivid cultural history. Duration: 101 MIN. After the documentary screening, we will have a small social dancing to honour the roots and feel the vibe of salsa! 🌈 Please read before getting your ticket: Baila Safica is a sapphic salsa & bachata social created to offer a safe, affirming space for sapphi

item.title: Make Better Notes: Keeping track of your ideas over time — Mon Nov 2, 6:30 PM — North York Central Library
item.description:
No matter what your interests, writing about what you read and experience can be both a pleasure and an essential tool for self-directed learning. In this program, attendees will learn the basics of two classic methods of making and organizing notes for long term use, the commonplace book and zettelkasten . These techniques can be employed through pen and paper or digitally through various free software. Attendees are encouraged to bring a laptop. Registration is encouraged. Drop-ins welcome until capacity is reached. item.title: How To Get the Most Out of the CRA's Website — Tue Nov 3, 2:00 PM — Wychwood
item.description:
A representative from the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) will provide an overview of CRA's digital services, including My Account, a secure portal that allows you to view your personal income tax and benefit information and manage your tax affairs online. Learn how to register for and use My Account to track your refund, view benefit and credit payments, update personal information, set up direct deposit, receive online mail, and access a variety of CRA services. Drop-in.
Source: Toronto Public Library — Young Adults

item.title: Computers for Beginners — Wed Nov 4, 2:00 PM — Bloor/Gladstone
item.description: Computers for Beginners is a 6-week course designed to build your confidence by introducing new skills slowly in a small, supportive community. At the end of the course, you may not know everything about the internet, but you will have a solid foundation of new skills and the confidence to continue learning. What Will You Learn? Basic tools such as the mouse and the keyboard How to search online for information, services and entertainment How to use email to keep in touch with family and friends Internet safety, security and privacy Week 1: Use the Mouse Week 2: Use the Keyboard Week 3: Use Windows Week 4: Use the Internet Week 5: Use Google Search & Maps Week 6: Use Email (Gmail) The class is limited to 8 participants. Registration is required, please register on the TPL website. If you need any assistance with registering, please visit us in-branch, or call us at 416-393-7674. item.title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online — Wed Nov 4, 8:00 PM
item.description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish **Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***
“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.
**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**
* Monday * Wednesday * Sunday
With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.
**Format** **Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)** Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:
* 2 native English speakers * 2 native Spanish speakers * 1 native speaker of another language
